author: NewsBreak
title: California Woman Sentenced to Five Years for Threatening Texas Federal Judge - NewsBreak
text:
4 hours ago Photo by Tingey Injury Law Firm on Unsplash AMARILLO, Texas – A California woman has been sentenced to five years in federal prison for threatening a United States District Judge in the Northern District of Texas, Acting U.S. Attorney Nancy E. Larson announced Wednesday.
Federal prosecutors said Dolly Patterson admitted to sending a threatening message on April 16, 2023, through an online “Contact Us” form directed at a judge based in Amarillo. The message read: “Tell that anti-abortion judge he better watch his back . . . for the rest of his life!”
Court records show Patterson acknowledged that the message, sent from California to Texas, was intended to be perceived as a genuine threat. She further admitted that her communication met the federal definition of a true threat to injure another person.
“The safety of our federal judiciary is paramount,” said Acting United States Attorney Nancy Larson. “Threats of violence to our judges are becoming all too common—whether made online or in person. Such threats are illegal and will be prosecuted.”
Authorities said Patterson pleaded guilty to transmitting an interstate threat, a federal offense. She was sentenced to the statutory maximum of five years in prison.
The case highlights growing concerns about threats against the judiciary, particularly those made across state lines. Prosecutors emphasized that Patterson’s actions, while carried out online from California, directly targeted a federal judge in Texas and will serve as a reminder that such threats carry serious consequences.
